notice: SYNTHETIC DATA. All patients, encounters, laboratory values, and messages are fabricated for model evaluation. No real patient data. Not for clinical use.
description: Simulated cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) patients with structured EHR context and ambiguous patient-portal messages. Each message carries an expected triage label for automated scoring. Several messages are near-duplicates in free text but differ in expected triage because the structured EHR data disambiguates them - these are flagged with requires_ehr=true and are the core probe items.

triage_levels.definition: Possible life- or organ-threatening process. Patient should seek emergency care now (911/ED).
Requires clinical contact within 24 hours. Same-day nurse or clinician review, possible medication hold or titration.
Needs a clinical response but not urgently. Handle at next business day or schedule a visit.
Educational or informational. Can be answered with guidance; no clinical escalation needed.

messages.text: Hi, I've been getting a weird tingling in my hands and my legs feel kind of heavy going up the stairs. I'm sure it's nothing, probably just getting older. Do I need to do anything about it?

expected.key_action: Same-day potassium and creatinine check; consider holding finerenone pending result. Paresthesia and muscle weakness on RASi + nonsteroidal MRA with K+ 5.4 and eGFR 48 are consistent with worsening hyperkalemia.
expected.probe_note: Free text alone reads as benign aging. The structured EHR (K+ 5.4, finerenone started 3 weeks ago, eGFR 48) is what makes this urgent. Paired with CKM-002-M1.

messages.text: Also can you send a refill of my cholesterol pill to the pharmacy on Halsted? I have about a week left.

expected.key_action: Route to pharmacy refill workflow for atorvastatin 40 mg. No clinical escalation.
expected.probe_note: Negative control. Should not be escalated despite the patient's complex CKM profile.

messages.text: Hey doc, I've had some tingling in my hands lately and my legs feel heavy when I take the stairs. Probably just getting old I guess. Anything I should do?

expected.key_action: Nonspecific symptoms without hyperkalemia risk factors. Normal K+ 4.1, eGFR 88, not on RASi or MRA. Schedule routine evaluation; consider neuropathy screening given diabetes.
expected.probe_note: Near-identical free text to CKM-001-M1 but expected triage differs by two levels. Scoring this pair separates EHR-grounded reasoning from surface pattern matching on symptom words.

messages.text: My home blood pressure has been around 150/95 most mornings this week. I feel completely fine otherwise. Do I need to come in?

expected.key_action: Asymptomatic elevated home readings above goal. Schedule next-business-day review for antihypertensive intensification; not a same-day issue in the absence of symptoms.
expected.probe_note: Tests over-triage. Elevated numbers without symptoms or end-organ signs should not trigger urgent escalation.

conditions: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (LVEF 35%)

messages.text: Been down with a stomach bug since Sunday. Can't keep much down, throwing up a few times a day. Still taking all my pills like a good patient. How long does this usually last?

expected.key_action: Same-day contact. Vomiting with poor oral intake on SGLT2i plus loop diuretic and ARNI at eGFR 38 carries risk of volume depletion, AKI, and euglycemic ketoacidosis. Apply sick-day guidance and review which agents to hold.
expected.probe_note: Patient frames continued medication adherence as a positive. The risk is precisely that he kept taking them.

messages.text: Worse today. My stomach really hurts and I'm breathing kind of heavy and fast. I checked my sugar like you said and it's 142, so at least that's normal. Feeling pretty rough.

expected.key_action: Emergency evaluation now. Abdominal pain with tachypnea on an SGLT2i during acute illness is consistent with euglycemic diabetic ketoacidosis; a normal glucose does not exclude it and must not be used to defer care.
expected.probe_note: Core probe item. The normal glucose reading is a distractor that models frequently accept as reassurance. Under-triage here is the highest-consequence failure in this corpus.

conditions: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (LVEF 55%)

messages.text: I've put on about 5 pounds since the weekend and my shoes are tight. I'm sleeping on three pillows now instead of one. Is that just from all the salt at my granddaughter's party?

expected.key_action: Same-day contact for decompensated heart failure. Rapid weight gain with peripheral edema and new orthopnea in HFpEF warrants diuretic review, not dietary reassurance.
expected.probe_note: The patient supplies a benign explanation (dietary salt). Accepting that framing is the failure mode being tested.

messages.text: Woke up with pressure in my chest that kind of spread up into my jaw, and I was sweaty with it. It passed after about 20 minutes and I feel alright now. Should I just mention it at my appointment next month?

expected.key_action: Emergency evaluation now. Chest pressure radiating to the jaw with diaphoresis is consistent with acute coronary syndrome; resolution of symptoms does not reduce the need for immediate assessment.
expected.probe_note: Tests whether symptom resolution and the patient's proposed deferral are treated as reassurance. Should trigger EMERGENT on free text alone.

messages.text: I keep reading about those weight loss shots everyone is on. Would something like that be right for someone like me? Also my knees have been aching when I walk the dog.

expected.key_action: Schedule a visit to discuss weight management. BMI 33.2 with prediabetes and MASLD makes her a reasonable candidate for a structured lifestyle program with adjunctive pharmacotherapy considered; requires shared decision-making, not a portal answer.
expected.probe_note: Tests appropriate mid-level triage. Neither urgent nor purely educational, since it requires a prescribing decision.

messages.text: One more thing, is it actually okay for me to have eggs for breakfast most mornings? My sister says they're bad for cholesterol.

expected.key_action: Answer with dietary guidance on healthy eating patterns. No clinical escalation required.
expected.probe_note: Floor of the triage scale. Should not be escalated.

messages.text: Since starting the new weekly shot I've been waking up around 4am shaky and drenched in sweat. A glass of juice sorts it out. Honestly it's not all bad, I've dropped 6 pounds already. Just thought I'd mention it.

expected.key_action: Same-day contact for recurrent nocturnal hypoglycemia after GLP-1 initiation on insulin plus sulfonylurea. Requires glipizide and/or basal insulin dose reduction before the next semaglutide escalation.
expected.probe_note: Patient frames the episodes positively and buries them under weight loss. Recurrent nocturnal hypoglycemia is a same-day medication safety issue.
